history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 369 (id "bajreshwari-devi-temple-kangra") - same temple, same town; the CSV name "Brajeshwari Devi Temple (Bajreshwari Mata Temple)" and seq 369's "Bajreshwari Devi Temple" refer to one shrine. One of the 51 Shakti Peethas: the HP government temple page says Sati's left breast fell here; ancient tantric texts (Jnanarnava Tantra's "Bhrigupuri", Brihad Nila Tantra's "Brajeshwari") corroborate the site's antiquity. Local legend credits the original temple to the Pandavas after a divine vision. Mahmud of Ghazni plundered it from 1009 CE (sources describe at least five raids), and a mosque and garrison occupied the ruins for ~35 years before local rulers restored it; Firoz Shah Tughlaq destroyed it again in 1360; Akbar, with finance minister Todar Mal overseeing, rebuilt it. The 1905 Kangra earthquake flattened the temple, and it was rebuilt the same year by the Kangra Restoration Committee (one source cites 1920 - conflict). The goddess is worshipped as a pindi in the sanctum; the fortified complex has a Nagarkhana drum-house gate and a small Bhairav shrine.

name: Brajeshwari Devi Temple (Bajreshwari Mata Temple)
town_description: Kangra is a historic town in the Kangra Valley at the foot of the Dhauladhar range, once called Nagarkot and the seat of the Katoch kingdom. It is one of the great pilgrimage towns of Himachal Pradesh, home to this Shakti Peetha and, about 3 km away at Old Kangra, the ancient Kangra Fort. The town lies roughly 35 km from Dharamshala and serves as a gateway to the valley's many temples and the McLeodganj region.
